label: Well-Adjusted Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents a group of 116 respondents characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their scores on all three psychological measures fall well below clinical thresholds, suggesting generally positive mental health and social connectedness. They report moderate daily screen or internet use of 1–3 hours.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily internet/screen use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.79), indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.28), well below clinical concern
Near-zero anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.04), suggesting emotional stability
Moderate and controlled internet/screen use (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment associated with structured daily routines

label: High-Distress Digitally Immersed Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (mean 1.72), PHQ-9 depression score (mean 1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety score (mean 2.14) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. With 181 respondents in the training split, this is a well-represented cluster characterized by the convergence of heavy digital engagement and broad mental health burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale (mean 1.72)
Endorses elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9 (mean 1.73)
Shows the highest anxiety levels among profiles on the GAD-7 (mean 2.14)
Engages in prolonged daily screen or internet use exceeding 5 hours
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests compounded psychological distress
tone: Distressed, emotionally burdened, and potentially socially withdrawn despite high digital connectivity

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging approximately 1.25, PHQ-9 depression scores around 0.81, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near 0.84, these individuals fall well below clinical thresholds across all three psychological distress measures, indicating generally positive mental well-being.

behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology, well below clinical concern
Demonstrates low anxiety levels consistent with healthy psychological functioning
